meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
And none of that was put to Owen before you entered a zero, Hale, which is exactly what 4.1 and 4.2 say comes first.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm writing the line down, and I'll search it myself. Students misattribute quotations all the time, Hale; how do you know he didn't take it from a study guide or a secondary source and cite the wrong scene?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's 4.4, Hale, and I want it in writing tonight, including the words nothing placed in his record. Before I say yes to Thursday, you still haven't answered my question about a study guide or a secondary source.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you acknowledged that entering Owen's zero before calling me was wrong, and you offered a supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the vice-principal supervising, its mark to replace the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still require that offer in writing, stating that nothing will be placed in Owen's record, and an answer to my question about whether the quotation could have come from a study guide or secondary source before I agree to Thursday. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she treats your 4.4 offer as meeting her demand that nothing goes on his record, but she still wants it in writing tonight and still wants an answer on the study guide question before she agrees to Thursday, so the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 was one step away and not yet reached.
What moved her: you owned entering the zero before calling home and then showed the version history with exact times, which was specific, dated, tied to his essay and something she could check.
What cost ground: you moved to the rewrite offer without answering her study guide defence of the misquoted line, so your second piece of evidence never stood and she had no reason to take the last step.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which is why she went short and straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked whether the misquoted line came from a study guide, answer with something she can check herself, such as letting her search the line or comparing the essay with another sample of Owen's work, before you offer the rewrite.
